correctness.rationale: The determinant factors exactly as \(64(T-X)(1-T-Y)(1-X-Y)\) for positive cyclic gaps. The gap-sum parity forces \(p,u,v\) either all integers or all half-integers. For integer \(p,u,v\), nonsquare \(u=v=0\) gives at most \(16\cos^2(2\alpha)\), while a nonzero defect gives \(D\le16\cos^6\alpha\), strictly below \(16\cos\alpha\cos(2\alpha)\) for \(0<\alpha=\pi/N\le\pi/8\). The half-integer branch has \(X,Y\ge\sin^2(\alpha/2)\), and the positive-factor product decreases in each variable. The quantized grid makes \(|T-1/2|\) smallest exactly for \(p=m\pm1/2\); equality in defect bounds forces \(|u|=|v|=1/2\). Thus every equality set is a one-vertex shift of a square and there are exactly \(2N\) distinct ones. The 825,642 numerical configurations over twelve grid orders corroborate but do not replace the all-order proof.

value.rationale: The sharp second-best cyclic D-optimal Fourier determinant after every orthogonal four-sample design is excluded is a natural extremal invariant. The theorem covers the infinite family \(4\mid N\) with all \(2N\) second-best sets, and a strict gap of asymptotic relative size \(5\pi^2/(2N^2)\), a meaningful sampling robustness scale. No arbitrary enumeration cutoff, speculative downstream theorem, or narrow table entry is needed to motivate the fact. Four consecutive characters are the basic higher-rank harmonic interpolation aperture; integer and half-integer gap constraints plus diagonal chord interactions give substantive structural analysis.
